explanation: Assumption: C++11 lambdas can capture any variable efficiently. Reality: C++11 standard captures only supported copy-by-value or capture-by-reference, making it impossible to move non-copyable resources (like `std::unique_ptr`) or large resources into the closure. Why It Fails: To circumvent this limitation, developers had to emulate move capture using `std::bind`. This technique binds the resource (after casting it to an rvalue via `std::move`) as an argument to a placeholder lambda. The resulting 'bind object' uses move construction to store the rvalue argument internally, thereby achieving resource ownership transfer into the callable object.
practical_example: A library developer writing C++11 code needs to pass a `std::unique_ptr` into a deferred execution function. Since direct capture fails, they wrap the lambda and the moved pointer in `std::bind` to ensure the pointer's ownership is correctly transferred to the resulting function object.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
